Tactile Maps Installed at MSP Airport Ease Travel for More Than Just Blind Passengers

2026-08-25 Matt Mikus, MPR News tactile maps, accessibility, MSP Airport, braille, 3D printing, blind passengers, disabilities advisory committee, universal design, airport navigation
Read the source article

Quick summary

Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport has become the first airport in North America to install custom 3D-printed tactile maps with braille and textures outside every bathroom, designed in collaboration with blind travelers to improve navigation for passengers with disabilities and everyone else.

Key takeaways

  • MSP Airport is the first in North America to install tactile bathroom maps with braille and textured surfaces
  • 146 bathrooms across two terminals require almost entirely custom maps — only two have identical floor plans
  • The airport coordinated with its Travelers with Disabilities Advisory Committee to develop designs and symbology
  • 3D printing with a local Bloomington company enabled quick prototypes and lower costs compared to traditional sheet metal
  • No Americans with Disabilities Act standards existed for tactile maps, so MSP created its own standards from scratch
  • Ken Rogers, president of the American Council of the Blind of Minnesota, served on the advisory committee
  • Airport staff hope to share their approach with other airports, with Portland already expressing interest
  • The maps benefit sighted travelers too, given the complexity of some MSP restrooms with multiple entrances
